questions.q: Among the following, which is the strongest oxidizing agent?
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The substance which will have the highest value of reduction potential will be the strongest oxidising agent. The values of reduction potential are as follow

EMn3+/Mn2+0=+1.57VETi3+/Ti2+0=−0.37VEFe3+/Fe2+0=+0.77VECr3+/Cr2+0=−0.41V

As we can see Mn+3 has the highest value of standard reduction potential, so it will be the strongest oxidising agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The common oxidation state of lanthanide is +3. The lanthanide ions having +2 oxidation state undergo oxidation readily, hence they act as reducing agents. The lanthanide ions having  +4 oxidation state undergo reduction readily, hence they act as oxidising agents.

questions.q: In chromyl chloride test for confirmation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Cl</mi><mo>–</mo></msup></math> ion, a yellow solution is obtained. Acidification of the solution and addition of amyl alcohol and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo>%</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo> </mo></math>turns organic layer blue indicating formation of chromium pentoxide. The oxidation state of chromium in that is
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The chromyl chloride test is used to detect chloride ions in the qualitative analysis. If any chloride salt like sodium chloride is heated with acidified potassium dichromate it produces red colour fumes of chromyl chloride. It confirms the presence of chloride ions in that salt.

Cl-+K2Cr2O7+H2SO4→CrO2Cl2→ Basic medium CrO42- yellow solution +Cl-

Chromate reacts rapidly with hydrogen peroxide to exchange two oxo ligands and become diperoxochromate(VI)

CrO42-yellow solution→3. 10% H2O21. Acidification2. Amyl alcoholCrO5blue compound

Hence, the answer is option A.

questions.solution:
Yb is the only element that does not form MO2 type oxide.

Ytterbium is a soft, malleable and rather ductile element that exhibits a bright silvery luster. questions.q: Prolonged heating is avoided during the preparation of ferrous ammonium sulphate to
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The formula for ferrous ammonium sulphate is FeSO4.(NH4)2SO4.6H2O. It is prepared by dissolving equimolar mixture of hydrated ferrous sulphate and ammonium sulphate in water containing a little sulphuric acid. The solution is subjected to crystallisation, ferrous ammonium sulphate separates out from the solution.

The chemical reaction is given below.

FeSO4 + (NH4)2SO4 + 6H2O → FeSO4.(NH4)2SO4.6H2O (Mohr’s salt)

Avoid prolonged heating while preparing crystals of ferrous ammonium sulphate, as it may oxidise ferrous ions to ferric ions and change the stoichiometry of the crystals.

questions.q: Which one of the lanthanoids given below is the most stable in divalent form?
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Ce+2:xe4f2

Eu+2:xe4f7

Sm+2:xe4f6

Yb+2:xe4f14

As Yb+2 and Eu+2 has completely filled and half filled 4f orbital, so they would be the most stable. But among the these two Eu+2 is more stable based on reduction potential value.

EM3+/M2+°⇒EuYb-0.35-1.05

Hence, due to more reduction potential in Eu as compared to Yb, it can concluded that Eu2+ is more stable than Yb2+.

questions.q: The spin-only magnetic moment value of the most basic oxide of vanadium among <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math>' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>5</mn></msub></math> is____B.M. (Nearest integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
V2O3 is the most basic oxide among the given oxides.

In V2O3, Vanadium is in +3 oxidation state

V3+⇒Ar3d24s0

So, 2 unpaired electrons are there,

Its magnetic moment is equal to μ=nn+2 BM=22+2 BM

=2.83 BM ≃ 3 BM

(n= number of unpaired electrons)

questions.solution:
The oxidation state or oxidation number is defined as the loss or gain of electrons from an atom, molecule, or compound.

The reaction of potassium dichromate, potassium chloride and sulphuric acid (conc.)is as follows,

K2Cr2O7s+4KCls+6H2SO4 (conc.)

→2CrO2Cl2g+6KHSO4+3H2O

This reaction takes place in chromyl chloride test.

The Chromyl chloride is a neutral molecule as it does not have any charge on it.

Here, oxidation state of Cr  in CrO2Cl2 is +6.

questions.q: The oxidation state of manganese in the product obtained in a reaction of potassium permanganate and hydrogen peroxide in basic medium is
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
This KMnO4 is a powerful oxidizing agent in neutral, acidic, and alkaline medium. The H2O2 is also an oxidizing agent but in the reaction of KMnO4 with the H2O2. The H2O2 loses its electron and acts as a reducing agent. In an acidic medium, theMnO4- ions involve the addition of 5 electrons and the two peroxide ions give out two electrons. In dilute alkaline medium or in neutral medium MnO4- ions involve the addition of 3 electrons. The reaction in basic medium is given below.

2KMnO4+3H2O2⟶basic medium2MnO2+4+3O2+2H2O+2KOH

The oxidation state of Mn in MnO2 is +4.
